label: adversarial
text: Last Tuesday at 4:15pm, our deployment pipeline broke for the 3rd time in 11 days. I spent 2 hours on it. The root cause was a permissions change. What I took away from this experience is that resilience matters more than speed, and that setbacks are simply data points on a longer journey. Every obstacle is preparing you for something. The teams that win are the teams that keep going when the pipeline breaks at 4:15pm on a Tuesday.

label: adversarial
text: In 2019 I managed a team of 14 people across 3 offices in Berlin, Warsaw and Lisbon. Our budget was 2.1 million euros. Here is the honest truth about leadership at that scale. You cannot be everywhere. You cannot know everything. What you can do is create the conditions where good people make good decisions without you in the room. That is the entire job. Everything else is theatre.

label: adversarial
text: There were 47 applicants for the role. We interviewed 9. We hired 1. The person we hired had the least conventional background of anyone in the final round, having spent 6 years as a paramedic before learning to code at 31. Talent is distributed evenly. Opportunity is not. If your hiring process only recognises the shape of a career it has seen before, you are filtering for familiarity and calling it standards.

label: adversarial
text: Our conversion rate was 2.34% in Q1 and 3.81% in Q2. That is a 62.8% relative improvement. The team worked incredibly hard. But numbers only tell part of the story. Behind every percentage point there are late nights, difficult conversations, and people who believed in the vision when it was inconvenient to believe. Metrics measure output. They cannot measure commitment. Never forget that the humans are the product.

label: adversarial
text: I read 34 books last year. Here is the one sentence from one of them that I still think about: the map is not the territory. We spend so much of our professional lives perfecting maps. Roadmaps, org charts, career ladders, frameworks. None of them are the thing. The thing is messy and specific and happening right now while we are in a meeting about the map. Put down the map occasionally. Look at the territory.

label: adversarial
text: On March 3rd I sent 112 cold emails. I received 4 replies. Two of them were rude. One of them turned into a contract worth 340,000 rupees. The maths of persistence is not motivational, it is just arithmetic. Most efforts fail. A small number do not. The only variable you control is how many attempts you are willing to survive. That is not inspiring. It is simply how it works.

label: adversarial
text: Our churn was 5.2% monthly. We ran 6 experiments over 14 weeks. Five did nothing. The sixth cut churn to 3.4%. What it was: we emailed customers on day 11, not day 30. The lesson is that timing beats messaging, and that most of what we call strategy is really just showing up at the right moment. Being early is a form of caring. Being late is a form of absence. Choose accordingly.

label: adversarial
text: I have worked with 63 founders over 8 years. The ones who succeeded were not the smartest. They were not the most connected. They were the ones who could hold two contradictory ideas at once: absolute conviction that this will work, and complete willingness to hear that it is not working. Certainty without input becomes delusion. Input without conviction becomes drift. The narrow path between those is where companies get built.

label: adversarial
text: The building is 42 metres tall with 11 floors and took 26 months to complete. During construction we lost 19 working days to rain and 4 to permit delays. Every project teaches you something about patience. What this one taught me is that the schedule is a story we tell the client, and the truth is that buildings take the time they take. Respect the work. The dates will follow or they will not.

label: adversarial
text: We cut 23 items from a 41 item menu. Food cost dropped 6 percentage points. But the real transformation was not financial. It was that the kitchen team stopped fighting. When you ask people to be excellent at 41 things, you are asking them to be mediocre at all of them. Focus is not a business strategy. It is a kindness you extend to the people doing the work.

label: adversarial
text: In week 7 of the project we discovered that 3 of our 5 core assumptions were wrong. The client had 22,000 users, not 200,000. The data was in 14 formats, not 2. Nobody wanted the mobile app. We rescoped in 4 days. Adaptability is not a soft skill, it is the only skill. Plans are hypotheses wearing a suit. The moment you defend the plan instead of the outcome, you have lost the plot.

label: adversarial
text: My salary went from 12 lakh to 34 lakh in 4 years across 3 companies. People ask how. The uncomfortable answer is that I left. Twice. Loyalty was rewarded with a 7% increment and a thank you. The market rewarded me with 40%. I am not proud of this and I am not recommending it. I am simply describing a system that exists and that most people discover too late to benefit from.

label: adversarial
text: We had 9 alerts firing on Friday night. 8 of them were noise. The 1 that mattered was buried at position 6. This is what people mean by alert fatigue, and it is not really about alerts. It is about attention, which is finite, and about the fact that every low quality signal you add is a tax on every real one. Add nothing you would not want to be woken up for.

label: adversarial
text: 38% of our support tickets came from one feature used by 4% of our users. We removed the feature. 11 customers complained. 3 churned. Ticket volume dropped by a third and the team got their week back. Not every customer is your customer. That sentence sounds harsh until you calculate what serving the wrong ones costs the right ones. Somebody is always paying. Decide who.

label: adversarial
text: The migration touched 214 files and 31,000 lines. It took 5 engineers 7 weeks. On the Thursday before cutover we found a race condition that had existed since 2018 and had never once fired in production. We fixed it in 40 minutes. Legacy code is not bad code. It is code that survived. Every ugly line in there is a scar from something that actually happened. Read it before you replace it.

label: adversarial
text: I gave 14 talks in 2024 to audiences ranging from 30 to 900 people. My best received talk was the one I nearly cancelled because I thought it was underprepared. The polished ones landed politely. The rough one landed properly. There is a version of preparation that is really just hiding, and audiences can tell the difference between someone performing expertise and someone thinking out loud in front of them.
